correctness.rationale: For 0<a<1 and (1-a exp(-2))/2<b<1/2, the odd invariant antidiagonal reduction has precisely two positive antipodal radii from monotonicity of h(s)=(s-1)exp(-s). The radius map is strictly increasing for r>=1 since G'(r)>1-a(e^-2+8e^-3)>0 and contracts in modulus for 0<r<=1; this proves all three global antidiagonal cases, not merely numerical sample orbits. At cycle points symmetric one-step multiplier a exp(-s)(2s^2-5s+1) has absolute value <1, antisymmetric multiplier -1+2as(s-2)exp(-s) is <-1 inner and in (-1,0) outer; zero multipliers a,a-2b are in (-1,1). Taylor at s=2 and logarithmic inversion establish both endpoint laws. The complete packaged standard-library checker passes 140 finite cases and four fold diagnostics, but finite computations are not used as proof.

originality.rationale: The originating 2023 article develops numerical bifurcation and critical-curve portraits but no exact low-gain antidiagonal basin theorem. The closest same-map 2026 theorem proves common compact absorption for -1/2<=b<1/2 but explicitly does not classify finite attractors/basins. The reused Lambert-W root count is algebraically equivalent to a fixed-point root count under b -> b-1, so novelty is not assigned to it. The new essential implications are the entire antidiagonal basin partition for all real x, the two-cycle Floquet saddle/sink split in the full plane, and simultaneous open basins of the origin and the outer two-cycle within a positive-coupling absorbing band.
